learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge about the fundamentals of automation and control methods.
Ability to interpret projects and technical reports.
Ability to evaluate the effectiveness, feasibility, and quality of implemented solutions.
Demonstrate the ability of analysis and synthesis.
Acquire the ability to solve problems effectively.
Express oneself correctly in Spanish, both orally and in writing.
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis, and processing within their field of application.
Information search and management skill.
Develop critical reasoning.
Develop the ability to work in a team.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Acquire the ability for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training.
Ability to generate new ideas (creativity).
Ability to work autonomously.
Motivation for quality and continuous improvement.
The general objective of the subject is for students to learn the fundamentals of automation and control methods.
Understand the technological realization of automation throughout history.
Understand the symbologies according to automation representation standards.
Represent, design, and interpret automation diagrams.
Solve basic automation problems using wired technologies: electrical, pneumatic, electro-pneumatic, and hydraulic.
Understand and use computer tools for the analysis, design, and simulation of automation systems.
Solve basic automation and industrial control problems using programmed technologies based on industrial programmable logic controllers (PLCs).

syllabus_topics: Introduction to automation and industrial control
Control with industrial programmable logic controllers (PLCs)

assessment_methods.method: Completion of assignments, questionnaires, exercises, problems, etc.

assessment_rules: To pass, the sum of all test scores must be greater than or equal to 5.0, and a minimum score of 40% of the value of each test is required. Students who fail the subject in the first call will only retake the tests they failed in the first call (i.e., those with a score below 50% of the test's value) in the second call. In all cases and calls, if a student does not meet any of the mentioned minimums, the overall grade for the subject will be calculated according to the UBU Evaluation Regulations.
